title: A Dropdown inside an errored FormGroup nests a second FormGroup and renders an empty alert
foundBy: session agent, while verifying the Form pattern fix for CUI-020
details: FormGroup forwards `error` to component children as a boolean, deliberately, so a design system control can paint its error border in sync with the message. Dropdown declares `error` as a string, the message to show. So a Dropdown inside a FormGroup with an error receives `error={true}`, reads it as a message, takes its chrome branch and renders a second FormGroup inside the first. That inner group renders `{true}`, and React renders nothing for `true`, so the page carries a live region that announces nothing. Measured in the Form pattern after a failed submit: six FormGroup elements for five fields, and five alert elements of which one is empty. The empty one is the nested group around the plan Dropdown. A screen reader meets an alert with no text, and the DOM carries a duplicated field wrapper. The fix is a judgement about which convention wins. Dropdown could treat a boolean error as paint the border and render no chrome, which keeps both props as documented. Or FormGroup could stop forwarding to children that declare a string error. The first is smaller and keeps each component's documented contract intact.

notes.text: Found because fixing CUI-020 made the error states reachable for the first time, so this had never been observable: no error ever rendered in that pattern. Anchors: FormGroup.tsx:77-78 forwards the boolean, Dropdown.tsx:31 declares the string, Dropdown.tsx:108 branches on truthiness.
